subhed: On Sunday, September 27, Swiss citizens will vote for or against the 'safeguarding of neutrality' initiative championed by the far right. Zala discusses the ambiguities of this principle which, more than a doctrine of foreign policy, has become a cornerstone of national identity.

title: Trump administration is trying to reshape election rules to its advantage ahead of midterm elections
subhed: The Supreme Court prevented Republicans on Friday from redrawing Missouri's electoral map to their benefit, but the party has managed to reshape districts in many other states. Meanwhile, the White House sought to purge voter rolls and limit mail-in voting.

title: E. Jean Carroll: The tenacious woman who brought down Trump
subhed: The writer and journalist filed two civil lawsuits against the former US president for sexual assault and defamation. In 'Not My Type,' she recounts the behind-the-scenes battle that she ultimately won.

title: 'Prize-contending author Orélien's AI controversy challenges the literary world's postcard image of the solitary writer'

We probably need to accept it, writes Le Monde's culture columnist Michel Guerrin.

title: How Paris, New York and Tokyo are all moving away from car-centric urban planning
subhed: In a study presented on September 9, the Paris Urban Planning Workshop analyzed how residents in seven major cities have been getting around over the past 20 years. The profound transformation of public space has given rise to new practices: residents walk, cycle and take public transport more.
